what.text: This page follows refugees from Ethiopia living in Sudan, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 47952 Ethiopian refugees in Sudan, 29.2% of all refugees from Ethiopia.
Sudan is the largest host of Ethiopian refugees, followed by Kenya, Uganda and South Africa.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over Eritrea territory in Ethiopia from 1964 to 1991, with the ELF and EPLF, and over the government of Ethiopia from 1976 to 1991, at war level in many of those years.
It also records armed conflict over the government of Ethiopia with the TPLF and GLF from 2020 to 2022, and over Oromiya territory with the OLA from 2019 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1967 at 28600 refugees.
The figure was at its highest, 856437, at the end of 1990, and the main years of displacement in the data are 1981 to 1990.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Sudan.
These are year-end totals for Sudan only, reported to UNHCR.
